question.problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+{\pi }^{2}},\,s>0
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t)\}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+{\pi }^{2}}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\pi }^{2}}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t)\}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}\{F(s)\} & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\pi }^{2}}\} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t).\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L\{f(t)\}=F(s)$, then

$$
L\{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ\}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}\{G(s)\} & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{F(s)}{s}\} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t).\end{aligned}
$$
